title: Pricing + packaging scratchpad v5
content:
Quick goal
- Back-of-envelope unit economics for hosted API and Dedicated tiers to validate headline price bands and where we should offer committed discounts / reserved capacity incentives.
- Capture key assumptions so we can iterate with infra/finance.

Top-level assumptions (feel free to update)
- Avg request: 350 tokens in + 350 tokens out => 700 tokens total per call (chat-heavy workloads). For embeddings use-case assume 100 tokens per request (one directional).
- Tokenization: our billing token ~= model token (uses tiktoken-like count). Keep simple.
- HW baseline costs (fully loaded):
  - Hosted GPU hot-path cost per GPU-hour (provisioned on avg across infra + overhead): $3.50/hr (proxy for v100/a10g-ish mix). TODO: confirm with infra.
  - Dedicated reserved cost (customer committed) effective infra cost: $2.40/hr (lower due to pooling + long term discounts).
  - CPU/other infra, storage, networking, SRE & infra ops overhead, support allocated: +30% on top of raw GPU cost.
- Throughput (tokens/sec per GPU, mixed models): assume 1200 tokens/sec for typical 8k context open models with our runtime optimizations at p99 batching.
- Effective tokens per GPU-hour = 1200 tokens/sec * 3600 sec = 4.32M tokens/hr.

Simple hosted cost-per-token (rough)
- Raw GPU cost per token = (GPU $3.50/hr) / 4.32M tokens = $0.00000081 ~ 8.1e-7 $/token
- Add ops overhead (30%) => multiply by 1.3 => 1.05e-6 $/token
- Add company margin + product ops + billing, aim target gross margin 60% => price = cost / (1 - margin) = 1.05e-6 / 0.4 = 2.63e-6 $/token (~0.00000263)
- Round to pricing-friendly: $0.000003 / token for hosted (baseline) => $0.003 / 1k tokens.

Sanity check: $0.003 / 1k tokens = $3 / M tokens. Our cost ~ $1.05 / M tokens => gross margin ~65% (okay).

Embeddings (different compute profile)
- Embedding model throughput higher (dense ops) => assume 10M tokens/hr per GPU -> cost/token smaller.
- Raw GPU cost per token = $3.50 / 10M = 3.5e-7; with overhead ~4.6e-7; price at 60% margin => 1.15e-6 $/token => $0.00115 / 1k tokens.
- We might price embeddings at $0.001 / 1k tokens (or $0.002 for managed indexing feature).

Dedicated / reserved pricing (unit economics)
- Effective infra cost per GPU-hour lower due to pooling: $2.40 + 30% overhead => $3.12/hr.
- tokens/hr same -> cost/token = 3.12 / 4.32M = 7.22e-7; price at 60% margin => 1.80e-6 $/token => $0.0018 / 1k tokens.
- Intent: offer committed customers ~30–40% discount vs hosted list. So if hosted is $0.003 / 1k, dedicated list might be $0.0018 / 1k.

Burst and overage considerations
- Dedicated customers will need burst capacity to avoid tailing requests -> premium for burst (e.g., burst credits or metered at hosted rate).
- Suggest commit tier pricing: commit X GPU-hours/month -> effective price P per 1k tokens; overage at hosted list.

Tier ideas (headline)
- Free tier: 100k tokens / month for dev + eval
- Starter (pay-as-you-go hosted): $0.003 / 1k tokens; no commit
- Growth: volume discount slabs (0–10M @ base, 10–100M @ -20%, 100M+ @ -40%)
- Dedicated Basic: reserved capacity (min 1 GPU equivalent) -> base $/1k tokens $0.0018
- Dedicated Pro: reserved + premium SLA + 24/7 support + additional retention/observability features -> $0.0012 / 1k (with 12mo commit)
- Private (on-prem/VPC): license + support (custom pricing) — goal to justify higher MRR and support fees.

Example customer math
- Chat-first app, 1M monthly active users, avg 1 chat/day, avg 700 tokens/call
  - tokens = 1M * 1 * 700 = 700M tokens/month
  - At hosted $0.003 / 1k => cost = 700k * $0.003 = $2,100
  - Wait math: need to be careful: 700M tokens = 700,000 * 1k tokens => multiply.
  - 700,000 * $0.003 = $2,100 (ok). Nice ROI if app monetizes >$X per DAU.

- High-throughput embedding pipeline: 50M embeddings (100 tokens each = 5B tokens)
  - 5B / 1k = 5,000,000 units * $0.001 => $5,000 (if embeddings priced $0.001 / 1k)

Areas of uncertainty / follow ups
- Confirm real-world tokens/sec for our most common models (gpt-like small/medium open models) with realistic batching distribution. Talk to infra/serving-runtime.
- Cost telemetry: get effective GPU/hr blended across cloud providers and spot vs reserved usage; ask finance for fully-loaded per-hour figure.
- Overhead estimates (30%) are rough; break out networking egress, storage, SRE, infra licensing, and account for multi-tenant security costs for hosted vs dedicated.
- SLA and SLO differentiation costs: quantize what extra ops-on-call cost is for Dedicated Pro.
- Evaluate price sensitivity via small experiment with customers: A/B hosted list price vs commit discount options.

Open questions to capture in pricing review
- Do we want to price per-token only or add per-request/ per-minute minima for very short calls? (helps voice/low-token chat abuse)
- Should embeddings have separate pricing surface (likely yes) and indexing as add-on?
- Reserved capacity packaging: price by GPU-equivalent or by tokens/month? (GPU-equivalent easier for us; tokens/month easier for customers)
- Do we offer guaranteed throughput SLAs per tier (and how to bill for missed SLOs)?

Random notes / quick heuristics for docs
- $/1k tokens is a simple headline for marketing.
- Convert to $/M tokens for enterprise conversations (multiply by 1000).
- Commit discounts should be expressed as % off list + effective $/1k for clarity.

Next steps
- Sync with infra to validate tokens/hr numbers (action: @Maya)
- Ask finance for fully-loaded GPU/hr and blended across clouds (action: @Jordan)
- Draft PR for pricing-proposals with 2 recommended sets: conservative (higher prices) and aggressive (aim to win share) and include sensitivity analysis.

Notes to self
- Keep the first public-facing pricing simple. Use tiers + clear committed discount table.
- Build calculator for customers (token estimator) on signup flow.

-- end --
